issue.title: middleware: a late timeout interrupt can stop the next call on the runtime
issue.body:
Found while checking internal/middleware for #3727's case. Each runtime there has one timer, reused for every call:

```go
in.timer = time.AfterFunc(time.Hour, func() {
	in.mu.Lock()
	if in.armed {
		in.fired = true
		in.rt.Interrupt(errTimeout)
	}
	in.mu.Unlock()
})
```

`armed` under the lock keeps #3727's case away: a func that gets the lock after disarm finds nothing armed, and an interrupt it gave before disarm is cleared there, so none sticks. But disarm's `in.timer.Stop()` doesn't wait for a func that has begun either, and nothing ties the func to the call it was set for. When a hook ends just as its time runs out, the func can still be on its way to the lock when the next call on that runtime arms. It then finds `armed` true and stops that call, which had its own time left: it reads "took too long" and its input goes on as it was. That call's disarm clears it, so it's one call, not every one after.

Which call that is depends on what runs next on the runtime: the next event's onEvent in a stream, often microseconds later, so that event reaches the agent as it was (a middleware that masks text lets that one through); another request's onRequest, onProvider or onResponse, since runtimes are pooled; or a strategy or onUsage, which share a runtime the same way. A module load that ends as its second runs out can leave one for the first hook too.

Reproduced at 1bb8143b with a 100ms pause put into the timer's func before it takes the lock, an onRequest that busy-waits 100ms, and requestLimit at 50ms for one request:

```
request before (250ms limit, 100ms of work): changed by its onRequest
request whose timer fires as it finishes (50ms limit, 100ms of work): changed by its onRequest
request after (250ms limit, 100ms of work): kept as it was, onRequest: took too long
request after that (250ms limit, 100ms of work): changed by its onRequest
```

When the pause ends while nothing is armed (the next request 200ms later), the requests after all go through, so it's the next arm that catches it. Without the pause it needs the func to run late by more than the gap to the next call, so it's rare: a hook that takes about its limit, on a busy machine. From outside it reads like #2565, #2687 and #2728, a hook that took too long, but the call it stops here had time left.

What I have in mind: when Stop says the func has begun, disarm waits for it before clearing, as #3727 does, so no func outlives the call it was set for and a call that ends in time pays nothing more. I'll take this one.

comments.body:
Fixed on a fork branch: `fix/3742-late-interrupt` (head `fd442d4f`, on upstream `6afbe3f3`) — a timeout's interrupt no longer lands on the next call.

**Root cause.** `internal/middleware/middleware.go`'s `disarm` set `armed = false`, read `fired`, unlocked and called `timer.Stop()` — it never waited for a function the timer had already started. `ClearInterrupt` could therefore land after the next `arm`, and the next call was interrupted for the previous call's timeout.

**Change.** the timer's func closes a `done` channel under `in.mu` when it ends; `disarm` waits on it when `Stop` reports the func had begun, then clears the interrupt. It is the same rule #3727 asks for in `agentplug.limit`; that one is a separate file and someone else's patch, so I left it alone.

**Verified.** Red: `go test -tags nogui ./internal/middleware/ -run TestLateInterruptSparesTheNextCall` → `late_interrupt_test.go:70: the second call: interrupted: took too long`
Green: `same command → PASS; `-race -count=2` green; package 31 tests pass` → `ok github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/middleware`

The test holds the timer's func in a synctest bubble, so it proves `disarm` doesn't return early rather than sleeping. Risk: a hook that blocked forever would now hold the call — the func only locks, interrupts and closes.

Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` over round 26's branches: 70 packages ok, 5 red (edit `TestWriteAtomicReadOnlyHardLink`, gateway's five, plugin `TestPluginSOCKSProxy`, provider's synctest fatal in `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials`, testenv `TestProgram`) — every one of them reproduces identically at base `6afbe3f3` in this environment (umask 0027), so none is from this change.

Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3742-late-interrupt — no PR opened, this repo takes no external PRs; say the word if you'd rather have the patch inline here.

issue.title: agentplug: a late timeout interrupt stays on the runtime and fails every later connect

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Found while going over #3673's agentplug test. `limit` in internal/agentplug/agentplug.go:

```go
t := time.AfterFunc(d, func() {
	fired.Store(true)
	a.rt.Interrupt(errTimeout)
})
err := fn()
t.Stop()
if fired.Load() {
	a.rt.ClearInterrupt()
	return errTimeout
}
return err
```

When the timer fires just as fn finishes, `t.Stop()` doesn't wait for the func that's already running. If that func hasn't called Interrupt yet when limit reads `fired` (or clears it), the interrupt lands on an idle runtime after limit has returned. moejs keeps an interrupt that arrives while nothing runs for the next call ("a host calls ClearInterrupt before reusing the runtime", in its Interrupt doc), so the agent's next Connect is stopped on entry. That call's own `fired` is false, so nothing clears it, and every Connect after fails the same way until the module is loaded again.

Reproduced at 27ca0bef with a pause put into the timer's func before `fired.Store`, a connect that busy-waits 100ms, and connectLimit at 50ms for one call:

```
connect before (1s limit): <nil>
connect whose timer fires as it finishes: <nil>
connect after, 1: connect: interrupted: took too long
connect after, 2: connect: interrupted: took too long
connect after, 3: connect: interrupted: took too long
```

Without the pause it needs the timer to fire within a scheduling slice of fn returning, so it's rare: a module that takes about its second, on a busy machine. Compile goes through the same limit, so a load can leave one for the first Connect too.

What I have in mind: the timer's func closes a channel when it's done, and when `t.Stop()` returns false limit waits on it before clearing, and returns errTimeout only when fn itself failed. I'll take this one.
